subject: gk
question: Which of the following changes CANNOT be reversed?

options.text: Blowing a balloon to increase its size till it is about to burst
Changing wet clothes to dry clothes
Rolling a roti from dough and baking it on a tawa
Stretching a rubber band and returning it to its normal size

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rolling a roti from dough and baking it on a tawa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Changes in a **substance **can take place in many ways.
 
• **Reversible change**: Change that can be **reversed** by **returning **to its** original state**.
 
 
• It might **change** how a substance **feels or looks** but it does not create** new substances**.
 
 
 
• **Irreversible change**: A change is **irreversible** when the change **can not** return to its **Original State**.
 
 
• **New substances** are **formed **in this type of **change**.
 
 
 
• **Rolling a roti from the dough and baking it on a Tawa** cannot be reversed as when roti is baked in Tawa the **chemical structure** of the roti **changes**.
 
 
• Thus with the **change** in its **chemical structure** renders the roti **irreversible**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blowing a balloon to increase its size till it is about to burst** is a reversible change as we can **return** the balloon to its **original state** simply by letting the **air in the balloon out **before it burst.
 
• **Changing wet clothes to dry clothes** is a **reversible change** as we can change the dry **clothes** to their **wet state** but simply **soaking them in water**.
 
• **Stretching a rubber band and returning** **it to its normal size** is a reversible change as it returns to its **original state**.
